items.why: Bach's cello suites in a recital hall.

listing.title: From Near Obscurity to Iconic Works: Bach’s Cello Suites
listing.description: The six suites for unaccompanied cello by Johann Sebastian Bach—once dismissed as mere curiosities—are now revered as iconic works. They are performed worldwide by cellists of all ages, and they are moreover prominently used in pop culture such as film and television as well as in expressions of humanitarian advocacy. In this special Focus on the Humanities talk, Edward Klorman illustrates how and why Bach conceptualized this highly innovative music and tells the unlikely story of how the Cello

items.why: Science talks with music.

listing.title: SoundWaves: Origins - The Spark of Life
listing.description:
In the 2026-27 academic year, SoundWaves is exploring Origins - from the start of the universe to how we developed language, join us for this four-part series as we uncover the origins of who we are. As always, each lecture is paired with live, musical performance as it relates to the theme of the evening.

In this second part, we are diving into the Spark of Life as we celebrate the 50th edition of SoundWaves. Topics include geochemistry, microbiology, and astrobiology!

items.why: A Grammy-winning jazz drummer at the Union Theater.

listing.title: Terri Lyne Carrington + Social Science
listing.description: Grammy and Doris Duke Award winner, NEA Jazz Master, and founder of the Berklee College of Music’s Institute of Jazz and Gender Justice, Terri Lyne Carrington has centered activism throughout her four-decade career as a drummer, producer, and educator, and earned the admiration of Herbie Hancock, Dianne Reeves, and Esperanza Spalding along the way. With her ensemble, Social Science, Carrington enters her next era of “story-filled groove-music” (NPR’s Tiny Desk) that merges crafted instrumentals, soulful R&B vocals, and poetic rap into consciousness-raising songs in the lineage of The Last Poets and Gil Scott-Heron. Come out for inspiring music that puts today’s world into perspective. Terri Lyne Carrington, drums Matthew Stevens, guitar Christie Dashiell, vocals Simone Bridges, MC/DJ Oliver Unger, bass Ian Macklin-Simms, piano Santiago Bosch Ogly, keys

items.why: A documentary screening.

listing.title: Exclusive film screening: "The New Gold Standard"
listing.description:
Interested in biomedical science? Cutting edge research techniques? Animal welfare?

Join us for an exclusive screening of "The New Gold Standard", a feature documentary by Steven Latham Productions. This film takes audiences inside some of the world’s leading research institutions to examine a scientific transformation already underway: the emergence of human-based research technologies that many scientists believe are reshaping how medicines are discovered, tested and approved.

items.why: A Cinematheque premiere.

listing.title: UW Cinematheque - Premieres
listing.description:
Cast: Anne-Laure Sellier
In the 1960s, an Italian Benedictine monk claimed to have invented a machine that allowed users to see into the past, as though on a TV set. While doing research, present-day academic Béatrice becomes fascinated by this “Chronovisor,” and plunges headlong into uncovering the truth about this mysterious device. This unusual and beguiling indie perfectly captures the sensation of going down a rabbit hole of dubious arcana.

listing.title: Dairy Air
listing.description:
@

What’s in the air we breathe every day? Get ready to explore the science of breathing as we learn about Wisconsin air quality and how our lungs help keep us healthy through crafts, games, and interactive activities. Depending on the day’s activities, you might walk through giant lungs, spin a prize wheel, or enjoy a lively puppet show along the way. Come discover more with us!
 

“Sharing our Dairy Air” program is funded by Sanofi as part of The Air We Share initiative

items.why: A Children's Museum music session for babies and toddlers.

listing.title: Li’l Music with Junko
listing.description:
Do you have a dancing baby? Discover Junko’s weekly music session where babies and toddlers can explore their natural love of rhythm. Together, you and your tiny dancer will bounce, sway, and rock with the music while learning simple rhythm patterns. They’ll build critical social skills over the weeks as they interact with new faces and watch the other babies in the room, and strengthen their bond with you through lap songs and movement activities.

It’s a wonderful way to get out of the house and connect with your baby or toddler through music and movement!

Leader Junko Yamauchi Stewart is a multitalented musician and educator, and founder of BENI Daiko Taiko Ensemble.
